question: A team has spent nine months on a feature and new research says users do not want it. What is the right question?
options: How to salvage the nine months
Whether the next month is worth spending
answer: The nine months are spent whatever happens next. Framing it as salvage is what turns a stopped project into a shipped one nobody uses, because it makes finishing feel like recovering rather than spending.
move: You cannot get spent time back by spending more of it.
trap: Nine months of work feels like something that can still be recovered.
